text:
support_lead: FYI — BrightLeaf is reporting a p99 regression on generation calls after the 03:10 UTC runtime deploy. They see p50 ~120ms, p95 ~380ms, but p99 jumped to ~1.8s. Customer is on Dedicated/enterprise. They attached traces and a small repro. They're blocked. :(

deploy-bot: deploy completed by @cheng at 2026-03-15T03:10:12Z commit abc1234 -> canary pool (runtime-v2.14.0) :rocket:

brightleaf_contact: thanks, here's a quick trace and repro: POST /v1/generate with prompt len ~560 tokens, concurrency 4. trace id: bl-rt-20260315-0315. We also see repeated KV cache misses in the trace.

cheng: Investigating. I'm seeing a sharp spike in prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate starting at 03:11:40. Dashboard excerpt: prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate 5m avg: 0.72 -> 0.95; evictions_per_min spiked 6x. p99 coincide with cache warmups.

cheng: Quick log snippet:
```
[03:11:43.342] prefix_cache: miss key=tenant:brightleaf:prefix:abcd123 len=64
[03:11:43.343] prefix_cache: insert key=tenant:brightleaf:prefix:abcd123 size=48B ttl=600s
[03:11:43.344] prefix_cache: evict key=tenant:brightleaf:prefix:xxxx999 reason=capacity
```

devon: Noticed a suspicious recent change in commit abc1234 (the canary). We changed cache key composition to include header `x-system-id` to support multi-tenant tracing. But we didn't normalize when header absent vs present -> lots of unique keys. Essentially the cache key entropy jumped.

devon: Repro locally by toggling that header: when header present key==tenant:brightleaf:prefix:abcd123:xsys:42, when absent key==tenant:brightleaf:prefix:abcd123. That doubles the key space for many requests (and some clients send random IDs).

nate: That would explain thrash. Eviction counts + miss rate align with newly-high cardinality key dimension. Two options: rollback canary or patch key normalization ASAP. For mitigation we can also temporarily bump prefix cache capacity and switch eviction policy from CLOCK-pro+ to LRU to favor recently used prefixes. But bumping capacity will increase mem use.

sally_prod: Customer SLA for BrightLeaf is high — they want a short RTO. Can we fallback their traffic to the pre-canary runtime?

cheng: Yes, we can re-route BrightLeaf to the stable pool for now. I'm going to create a route rule to pin their org-id to stable nodes. Command (ops internal API):
```bash
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/routing/rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"org_id":"brightleaf","route":"stable-runtime"}'
```

ops-bot: rollback route rule applied for org brightleaf -> stable-runtime at 2026-03-15T03:18:05Z :white_check_mark:

support_lead: Great, customer saw immediate drop in observed p99 after we moved them. But we still need a fix in code and a plan so this doesn't recur.

devon: Working on a small patch to normalize keys: strip `x-system-id` unless header is explicitly flagged as cache-relevant, and fallback to canonical form. Patch diff snippet: 
```diff
- key_parts.append(headers.get('x-system-id'))
+ if headers.get('x-system-id') and headers.get('x-system-id') in ALLOWED_SYSIDS:
+   key_parts.append(headers.get('x-system-id'))
```

devon: Also adding a unit test for key uniqueness and a metric alert for sudden increases in cache key cardinality.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: runtime-v2.14.1 by @devon at 2026-03-15T03:48:10Z

cheng: After canary (03:50 UTC) observed metrics: prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate dropped to ~0.18 on canary hosts; evictions_per_min back to baseline. For BrightLeaf pinned to stable we saw p99 drop from 1.8s -> ~420ms within a minute of route change.

nate: We also temporarily increased prefix cache size from 8GB -> 12GB in canary to give immediate headroom while patch rolls out cluster-wide. Command used:
```json
{"service":"prefix-cache","capacity_bytes":12884901888}
```

devon: Patch merged to main at commit def5678. Plan: roll runtime-v2.14.1 to canary -> gradual -> full over 2h with key-normalization and unit tests. Also added guardrail: reject keys with random-looking x-system-id (>40 char or non-alnum) and metric for key-cardinality > 10k/min per tenant.

support_lead: Customer notified and on the stable route for now. Ops to monitor. BrightLeaf replied: "Thanks — p99 back to acceptable. We'll keep an eye on edge cases." :relieved:

sally_prod: Postmortem items (high level):
- Root cause: cache key entropy increase due to header inclusion without normalization (dev regression)
- Immediate mitigations: route brightleaf to stable, canary patch, bump canary cache capacity
- Long-term fixes: key normalization, unit tests, cardinality alerting, deploy checklist update to include cache-key-change review

nate: Action items (owners):
- devon: PR for key normalization & tests (done)
- cheng: rollout v2.14.1 to remaining clusters (in progress)
- eng-sre: add cache-key-cardinality alert to critical dashboards (ETA 24h)
- support: update SLA notes and send follow-up message to customer (ETA 2h)

devon: Quick note — also uncovered an unrelated TTL bug where some prefix entries were set with ttl=0 on cold path. Filed a separate issue #4567.

support_lead: Closing loop — will follow up with BrightLeaf once full roll completes. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
